ac: Our students engage in powerful, real-world learning through HEAT, a place-based program that connects students with leaders in Healthcare, Energy, Education, Environment, Agriculture, and Technology. Once a month, students spend the school day at partner sites across NYC, working alongside professionals, NYCPS teachers, and peers from other schools. Through design thinking, entrepreneurship, and social justice lenses, students explore complex challenges and develop industry-informed projects. Each student earns 2 academic credits, financial literacy skills, and a stipend. In Spring 2024, we launched a transformative Civic Readiness course rooted in civil rights history. Students explored the legacy of the Freedom Riders through research, interviews, and project-based learning. The course culminated in a six-day trip retracing the Freedom Riders' journey from JFK to Atlanta and through key sites of the 1960s civil rights movement. This experience fostered deep reflection on kindness, courage, equity, and civic responsibility. We also offer a wide range of after-school and summer enrichment activities such as Art, Theater, Robotics, Video Game Club, Fitness Club, Soccer, Karaoke, and more. These experiences nurture student interests, talents, and community connections year-round

ac: At Brooklyn Community High School for Excellence and Equity, we provide a dynamic range of extracurricular and enrichment opportunities that extend learning beyond the classroom and reflect our commitment to equity, student voice, and real-world readiness. Students engage in hands-on, interest-driven learning through a variety of clubs that foster creativity, wellness, and innovation. The Hydroponics & Agriculture Club builds on our Hydroponics Certification program, allowing students to explore sustainable farming, food justice, and environmental stewardship. Our Open Art Club and Next Generation Media Arts programs offer creative outlets for visual arts, digital storytelling, and multimedia production, aligning with our TV production and technology pathways. To support physical and mental well-being, students participate in Martial Arts and Yoga, promoting discipline, mindfulness, and healthy lifestyles. We integrate enrichment with academic and career preparation through programs such as CDOS, College Now, HE3AT, and our School Technology program, which provide early college exposure, technical skill development, and industry-recognized certifications. Career pathways in cosmetology, workforce development, and healthcare-related fields (such as Home Health Aide training where applicable) offer students opportunities to pursue licensure and direct employment after graduation. Students gain valuable real-world experience through structured opportunities such as HE3AT place-based internships, Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP), and Work, Learn & Grow (NYCDOE). These experiences help students build professional skills, explore career interests, and connect academic learning to authentic workplace environments. We empower students to lead and advocate for their community through Student Government, fostering civic engagement and leadership skills aligned to the Seal of Civic Readiness. Programs such as the Freedom Writers Initiative and our comprehensive Writing Program promote literacy, identity development, and student voice. Additionally, Study Skills workshops and targeted literacy and math interventions ensure that every student receives the support needed to succeed academically.
